title: Reference-erasure tolerance at scale and the unknown-support identifiability bridge
question: Does the Thread-F erasure tolerance (cogirth - 1) of the leaf-report matroid stay at zero across real reference trees, or was the single 1322-leaf measurement an artefact of one tree?
Does the fibre-dimension law |P| - s hold on real trees at scale?
With the support UNKNOWN, how many references can be erased before more than one minimum-size support explains the observations, and does the known-support theory predict that threshold?

plan.survey: Every exactly explainable bank case (support = generating support, R = observed references) plus random supports of K in {3,5,10,12} on every positivity-conformant frozen panel, 5 replicates per (panel, K, mode) with mode in {any edge, internal edge only}.
checks: modular rank identity rank = s + 1 under two primes
unreduced dynamic program vs branch-collapsed dynamic program
exhaustive erasure of observed-leaf subsets (brute force) wherever at most 40000 subsets are needed
independent component recomputation of every DP witness
plan.bridge: exact_biotrees K=2 with |R| <= 130, exact_10k K=3 and exact_biotrees K=3 with |R| <= 45; removal regimes random (2 seeds), whole_clade (2 seeds), adversarial_nearest; up to 14 erasures, stopping 3 steps past the first failure.
bridge_checks: every minimum-size support confirmed by the exact rational Stage25/42 endpoint polytope oracle
minimum size cross-checked against the frozen solve_partial solver at the full panel
exhaustive exact enumeration (no prefilter) as ground truth on every case with at most 90 edges

limits.threshold_search: exponential bracketing then bisection, both endpoints evaluated

caveats: The 1322-leaf public tree of Thread F had negative ANI branch lengths floored upstream at 1e-4 and its fitted reports are synthetic exact-model values; the same holds for every exactly explainable bank case. Statements here are about real tree geometry with synthetic exact observations, not about biological recovery from measured distances.

Panels carry no mixtures, so panel supports are drawn at random; because s and the cogirth depend only on topology and support and not on the edge metric, this is a statement about real tree topology.
The erasure tolerance and the fibre dimension are metric invariant; the unknown-support threshold is not, since it depends on the observed values.
